artifacts.summary: Determines that verify-deploy.sh carries no source-store invocation refusal at all (confirmed byte-identical output both ways); only check-extension-docs.sh and sync-manifest-scripts.sh actually refuse via deploy-root-guard.sh, and the refusal is not load-bearing for correctness (REPO_ROOT=$(pwd) override, already documented in both scripts' headers, produces output identical to the deployed-copy invocation). Recommends resolution (a): self-correcting default root resolution (git rev-parse --show-toplevel fallback) scoped to the two affected scripts only, leaving deploy-root-guard.sh's ~115+ other callers untouched.

memory_candidates.content: agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/deploy-root-guard.sh is sourced by ~120 scripts to catch a '../..' root-resolution bug that only fires when a script resolves REPO_ROOT relative to its own BASH_SOURCE and is invoked from the 4-levels-deep source store (agent-system/extensions/<ext>/scripts/) instead of the 2-levels-deep deployed tree (.claude/scripts/ or .opencode/scripts/). Several callers (check-extension-docs.sh, sync-manifest-scripts.sh, validate-context-index.sh, measure-eager-context.sh, generate-context-line-counts.sh) already document a working bypass: `REPO_ROOT=$(pwd) bash agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/<name>.sh`. Before assuming the guard is load-bearing for a given caller, test empirically whether REPO_ROOT=$(pwd) from the source-store path produces output identical to the deployed-copy invocation -- for at least two confirmed scripts it does, meaning the guard there is purely a diagnostic nicety, not a correctness requirement.

When a task dispatch names a cluster of scripts as sharing one defect (e.g. 'three scripts refuse to run from X'), verify each one individually before assuming the group description applies uniformly -- a verification *line* in an originating task's plan can bundle scripts together (e.g. `verify-deploy.sh/check-extension-docs.sh/sync-manifest-scripts.sh`) even when only a subset actually exhibits the behavior. The originating task's own progress/issue artifacts (phase-N-progress.json, issues.jsonl) are often more precise than the summary that gets forwarded into a follow-up task's description.
